title: The portability job's Windows scope expires when the transport lands
description:
A standing constraint with an expiry date, filed so it is revisited deliberately rather than either 'fixed' early or forgotten.

The persona-core-must-stay-portable memory (commit 34c4e4a) records: the CI portability job cross-checks x86_64-pc-windows-msvc against hire-core ONLY, and explicitly says do NOT add --workspace for Windows, because hire-grpc is Unix-only by design. Makefile 'portability' mirrors it.

That reasoning is correct TODAY and becomes wrong the moment persona-vvs2.4 lands a named pipe transport. At that point hire-grpc is no longer Unix-only by design, and the cross-check that was deliberately narrow becomes accidentally narrow -- it would stop catching exactly the drift it exists to catch, silently, with nothing failing.

So: when the transport work lands, widen the Windows target to --workspace and update that memory, or record why not.

THE OTHER HALF OF THAT MEMORY DOES NOT EXPIRE and should not be swept up in the change: do not propose a windows-latest RUNNER instead of the cross-check. hire-core's tests are byte-exact arithmetic with no platform-dependent behaviour, so running them on Windows proves close to nothing that compiling them does, and drift is the failure worth catching. Whether that stays true once hire-grpc compiles for Windows -- where there IS platform-dependent behaviour in the transport, the DACL and the pipe semantics -- is a separate question this bead should also answer. It is the first Windows code with behaviour worth executing.

Note step 1 of the epic's suggested order, a Windows CI leg for hire-core, is ALREADY DONE in 34c4e4a. This bead is its successor, not a duplicate.
acceptance_criteria: When the named pipe transport lands, the portability target scope is widened or a recorded reason given; the persona-core-must-stay-portable memory updated to match; a decision on whether Windows now warrants an executing runner.
